prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

1914 The phantoms flit before our dazzled eyes, Glory and honour, wrath and righteousness, The agèd phantoms in their bloodstained dress, Vultures that fill the world with ravenous cries, Swarming about the rock where, chained apart, In age-long pain Prometheus finds no rest From the divine flame burning in his breast, And vultures tearing at a human heart. Not yet the blessed hours on golden wings Bring to the crucified their sure relief, Deeper and deeper grows the ancient grief, Blackest of all intolerable things. Eternal Rebel, sad, and old, and blind, Bound with a chain enslaved by every one Of the dark gods who hide the summer sun, Yet art thou still the saviour of mankind. Free soul of fire, break down their chains and bars, Drive out those unclean phantoms of the brain, Till every living thing be friends again, And our lost earth true comrade to the stars.

Here are two ways to polish the text, depending on your intended format:

### Option 1: Elegant Prose (Ideal for essays, speeches, or professional articles)

> **1914**  
> Spectral illusions flit before our dazzled eyes—glory, honor, wrath, and righteousness. These ancient specters, clad in bloodstained garments, resemble ravenous vultures that fill the world with their frantic cries. They swarm around the solitary rock where Prometheus, eternally bound, finds no respite from the divine flame burning within his chest, even as these vultures tear at a human heart.

> 
> May this free, unyielding spirit of fire break its chains and bars, dispelling these corrupting delusions of the mind until every living creature is reconciled in friendship, and our lost Earth is restored as a true comrade to the stars.

---

### Option 2: Refined Verse (Preserves the poetic structure with heightened lyrical elegance)

> **1914**  
> 
> Phantoms flit before our dazzled eyes—  
> Glory, honour, wrath, and righteousness,  
> Ancient specters in their bloodstained dress,  
> Vultures filling earth with ravenous cries,

outputs.L2:
In the year 1914, ancient and blood-soaked illusions dance before our dazzled eyes—notions of fame, dignity, anger, and moral righteousness. These persistent ghosts act like screeching, ravenous birds of prey that swarm across the globe. They cluster around the solitary cliff where Prometheus remains trapped in endless torment, suffering both from the sacred fire burning in his chest and from vultures tearing away at his human flesh. 

A merciful rescue on golden wings has not yet arrived to offer relief to this tormented figure. Instead, this primal sorrow steadily deepens, becoming the darkest and most unbearable of all agonies. 

Although this immortal dissident is sorrowful, ancient, sightless, and fettered by every shadowy deity that blocks out the warm sunlight, he remains the ultimate redeemer of human race. 

O untamed spirit of flame, shatter these physical restraints and expel these corrupted delusions from our minds! Grant us a time when every living creature lives in harmony once more, and our strayed planet is restored to true companionship with the stars.
outputs.L3:
**The Fire Unbound: A Reflection on War, Suffering, and Human Redemption**

Throughout history, the brutal machinery of war has been fueled not merely by hatred, but by the insidious illusions of glory, honor, and self-righteousness. These false virtues act like predatory vultures, circling above humanity and feeding upon its conflicts. Masquerading as noble ideals, they drive nations into destructive violence, transforming sacred human life into prey for an unquenchable desire for dominion.

In this ongoing tragedy, humanity finds its ultimate archetype in the figure of Prometheus. Suffering as the tormented embodiment of the human spirit, mankind endures a continuous, agonizing punishment. Just as the mythical eagle preyed upon the Titan, the destructive forces of war and delusion tear relentlessly at the heart of humanity, inflicting wounds that bleed across generations.

Tragically, relief from this intense ordeal has yet to arrive. Age after age, the cycle of conflict repeats, causing humanity’s ancient grief to deepen into a profound, historical trauma. The weight of unalleviated pain presses heavily upon the collective soul, leaving a world weary of endless sacrifice and longing for a respite that perpetually seems to elude its grasp.

Yet, despite being bound and subjugated by these dark forces, all hope is not lost. The rebellious Promethean spirit—though chained—remains the ultimate savior of mankind. It is this indomitable spark of defiance, truth, and compassion within the human character that refuses to be completely extinguished by tyranny and deceit. Even in bondage, it holds the sole key to our liberation.

Ultimately, an impassioned plea rises up to this free, fiery spirit: break the heavy chains of bondage and rise once more. May this untamed flame banish the harmful delusions of false glory that have plagued the Earth for millennia. By shattering the myths that justify violence, the Promethean spirit can finally heal the world's ancient wounds and restore a lasting peace and harmony to all mankind.
outputs.L4:
**I. The Iron Crag of 1914**

The year turns black upon the calendar of time;
A shadow falls across the fertile, quiet fields.
In nineteen-fourteen, the world is dragged in chains
To the bare, frozen summit of a modern doom.
Here stands Mankind—not a king, but a prisoner,
Bound by heavy links of steel to the jagged crags of war.
Below, the trenches stretch like open, bleeding wounds,
And the earth groans under the tread of marching millions,
Duped into believing that their sacrifice is sacred,
Their agony a holy offering to the gods of state.

**II. The Vultures of False Glory**

High above the bound titan, dark wings eclipse the sun.
They descend in a screeching storm—the vultures of false glory.
Beaks dripping with the rhetoric of honor and triumph,
They tear at the exposed heart of vulnerable humanity.
Their feathers are painted with the banners of nations;
Their talons are forged from propaganda and righteous lies.
"Die for the Fatherland!" they cry, "Suffer for the Empire!"
With every plunge of their cruel talons, they feast upon
The marrow of youth, the promise of the future,
Leaving behind only the agony of the rotting fields.
These are the oppressive mental chains—the deep delusions
That convince the sufferer that his bondage is his duty,
And his destruction, his noble crown.

**III. The Fire Reawakens**

Yet deep within the breast of the chained titan,
Beneath the wounds, beneath the blinding smoke of artillery,
There lingers a spark that cannot be extinguished.
It is the ancient spirit of Prometheus—the fierce, unyielding rebel,
The bearer of light who dared to defy the tyrant gods.
Invoke him now! Call forth that indomitable, fiery soul!
For fire alone can melt the iron forged by deception;
Reason alone can sever the ideological chains.
Let the rebel spirit awaken in the hearts of the deluded mass!
Let them see that the true enemy sits not across the wire,
But in the high towers where war is plotted,
And in the minds that bow to the myth of righteous slaughter.

**IV. The Dawn of Universal Peace**

With a sudden, thunderous surge of awakening truth,
The titan strains against his ancient fetters.
The Promethean flame bursts forth from his broken hands,
Blinding the black-winged vultures of false glory.
With a shriek of terror, the birds of prey flee into the dark,
Their illusions shattered by the unbearable light of reality.
The iron chains snap like dry twigs; the crag collapses.
The fog of war lifts from the scarred and weeping earth,
Exposing the lies that drove brother to murder brother.
In the warmth of this liberated fire, humanity stands upright,
Banishing the bloody madness of war forever,
And weaving, upon the healed soil of the world,
A grand and universal mantle of eternal harmony and peace.
outputs.L5:
For centuries, humanity has tied the concept of glory to the golden armor of conquerors, the roar of triumphant armies, and the monuments built to outlive time. We look for greatness in the bright, untarnished flashes of life. Yet, high above the dust of fallen empires, riding the thermal currents of an indifferent sky, fly the true, silent inheritors of the earth: **the vultures**.

To the untrained eye, there is no **glory** in a creature that waits for death. The vulture has long been burdened by human prejudice, vilified as a grotesque harbinger of doom, a grim shadow lingering at the edges of mortality. But to view them only through the lens of decay is to miss the magnificent poetry of their existence.

Watch them as they rise. Without a single flap of their broad, dark wings, **vultures** catch the rising heat of the morning sun, spiraling upward into the stratosphere. In the air, all awkwardness vanishes. They move with an effortless, majestic grace that mocked the gravity binding the creatures below. They are master navigators of the wind, surveying vast horizons with unmatched patience and sharp, discerning eyes.

And what is their purpose? While kings fight and bleed for fleeting pride, the vulture fulfills a solemn, vital duty. They are nature’s ultimate cleansers, the guardians of balance. Where disease and pestilence would rot the earth, the vulture descends, transforming ending into renewal. They ask for no praise, build no temples, and wage no wars, yet they perform a service without which ecosystems would collapse.

There is a profound, shadowed glory in that quiet resilience. They do not fear the end of things; they understand it. They know that all mortal ambitions—every crown, every battlefield, every empire—eventually settles into silence beneath the open sky. 

When the noise of human pride finally fades and the dust settles over our forgotten achievements, the sky will still belong to them. High above the ruins of tomorrow, **the glory** of the **vultures** will endure—soaring on the wind, patient, majestic, and entirely untouched by time.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a classic early-20th-century style anti-war poem titled "1914" that uses the myth of Prometheus as an allegory for humanity's suffering.
counterfactuals.output:
**1914**

We stole the fire. We thought the flame divine,
A light to guide the march of mortal men;
In steel and steam we built a sacred shrine,
And swore we should not walk in night again.
We seized the secrets of the quiet skies,
And deemed ourselves as gods upon the earth,
With clever hands and proudly lifted eyes,
Unknowing what our stolen spark was worth.

Then August struck the flint. The heavens broke,
And for our pride, the ancient wrath awoke.

Now bound upon no mythic mountain height,
Nor chained to marble peak in Caucasus,
A generation bleeds in winter’s light,
Where cold and iron wire encircle us.
The mud of Flanders is our barren rock,
The narrow trench our altar of despair,
Where shivering thousands wait the dawn’s dark shock,
And breathe the sulfur in the heavy air.

Down swoops the eagle—not of bone and feather,
But forged of high explosive, brass, and lead;
It screams across the ruined autumn weather,
To tear the living and defile the dead.
With iron beak it rips the helpless side,
It feeds upon the vitals of the young;
In smoke and flash the terrible divide
Of soul and broken flesh is wildly wrung.

And through the night, beneath the flare-lit skies,
The tormented flesh re-forms in fitful sleep;
The shattered boy comes to himself, and cries,
Re-made to suffer, and re-made to weep.
For dawn will bring the iron bird once more,
To rend the heart that mended in the dark—
An endless cycle on a bloody shore,
The bitter payment for the stolen spark.

O Titan World! Was this the grand design?
To turn our wisdom into screaming shells?
To drag the noble to the slaughter-line,
And build a thousand brief, terrestrial hells?
The old gods laugh above the smoke and mire,
While man, the godlike, perishes in fire.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a poem about the outbreak of World War I.
counterfactuals.output:
The summer came with golden light,
In nineteen-fourteen, warm and bright.
Across the fields of wheat and grain,
No whisper spoke of coming pain.
The cities slept in cultured pride,
While rivers drifted, deep and wide,
And Europe basked in tranquil sun,
Unaware of what was soon begun.

Then through Sarajevo's street,
Amid the dust and stifling heat,
A pistol flashed, a shot rang clear,
That struck the royal heir with fear.
Two bullets severed peace in twain,
And flooded empires with disdain;
A spark fell on a dry estate,
Unlocking heavy doors of fate.

Like dominoes of steel and lead,
The hidden treaties started red.
From St. Petersburg to Berlin’s spire,
The secret pacts pulled fatal wire.
Mobilization orders signed,
As statesmen, deaf and proud and blind,
Surrendered to the iron wheel
Of railway clocks and marching steel.

They cheered the trains with foolish joy,
Each mother’s unsuspecting boy.
With flowers stuffed in rifle barrels,
They sang their patriotic carols.
"Back home before the leaves shall fall!"
Echoed the blind, triumphant call.
They marched to war with banners high,
Beneath an unremembering sky.

Sir Edward watched from London’s height,
As dusk consumed the fading light.
"The lamps go out across the land,
Turned off by an immortal hand;
We shall not see them shine again,"
He murmured for the doomed young men.

The golden summer bled away,
Into a cold and muddy grey.
The world they knew was blown apart,
To break a generation's heart,
As barbed wire rose and cannons roared,
And darkness swept upon the sword.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Compose a poem in formal verse exploring how traditional notions of glory and honor act like vultures preying on the human spirit, featuring imagery of chains, fire, and cosmic redemption.
counterfactuals.output:
The gilded brass and trumpets sound on high,
To name as holy what is born of blood;
While in the shadows of a darkened sky,
Great carrion wings descend upon the mud.

For Honor weaves a cold, relentless chain,
And binds the spirit to a martial vow;
We wear the iron links of ancient pain,
And place the heavy laurel on the brow.

A fierce, unflagging fire consumes the heart,
Fed on the fuel of a noble lie;
It tears the quiet, tender soul apart,
To light a beacon where the foolish die.

The dark-winged raptor picks the spirit bare,
Where empty banners flutter in the dust;
It feeds upon the marrow of despair,
And turns our golden monuments to rust.

Yet far beyond this dark and bloody sphere,
Where star-born flames redeem the spirit’s pain,
The soul unbinds its chains of pride and fear,
And breaks forever from the vulture’s reign.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Can you write a tragic, dramatic poem titled "1914" contrasting the dark gods of war with the "Eternal Rebel" Prometheus, ending on a hopeful plea for universal peace?
counterfactuals.output:
**1914**

The summer dies; the iron trumpets blow,
Across the continent the shadows spread.
The year is nineteen-hundred and fourteen,
And earth prepares her banquet for the dead.
A sudden madness grips the minds of men,
As millions march into the hungry night,
Unknowing that the world they used to love
Is smothering its last and gentle light.

From abyssal gloom, the dark gods rise again,
With eyes of brass and throats that thirst for gore.
Old Moloch smiles, and Ares takes the reign,
To reignite the ancient lust for war.
They crave the shrapnel, mud, and shattered bone,
They crown the tyrant, sanctify the spear,
And feed upon the weeping of the world,
Transmuting human grace to blindest fear.

Yet bound upon his cold and jagged peak,
Where eagles tear his ever-bleeding side,
Stirs Prometheus, the Eternal Rebel soul,
Who views the tragedy with tragic pride.
He stole the sacred spark from heaven’s height,
Not for the mortar, gas, or bayonet,
But so humanity might build and dream,
In dignity that heaven could not fret.

"Is this my gift?" the noble Titan cries,
As sulfur clouds obscure the stars above.
"I gave you flame to warm your shivering hearths,
To light the paths of reason, art, and love!
The dark gods twist the sacred glow I brought,
They turn my fire to a scorching curse!"
Yet still he defies the masters of the slaughter,
Unbowed within a darkening universe.

Oh, Eternal Rebel! Hear our desperate prayer!
Cast down the dark gods from their bloody height!
Quench the cruel inferno of this war,
And bless the earth again with holy light!
Let from the trenches of this tragic year
A final, sacred covenant release:
That man shall lay his iron weapons down,
And dwell forever in universal peace.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a poem criticising the glorification of war in 1914 and calling for the human mind to break free from destructive illusions.
counterfactuals.output:
They marched beneath an August sky,
In summer’s heat and polished leather,
With brass bands blaring out the lie:
That youth and sacrifice together
Were sacred gifts a man should bring
To serve a myth, a flag, a king.

They wove a spell of knightly grace,
Of romantic steel and noble strife,
And masked the horror of the place
That traded innocence for life.
They sold the grave as victory’s bed,
And crowned with bays the shattered dead.

How easily the mind succumbs
To hollow words and thunderous drums,
To ancient specters carved in stone
That feed on marrow, flesh, and bone!
A fever born of pride and state,
That paints as honor what is hate.

Oh, grand delusion of the brave,
That turns the earth into a grave!
What glory lies in mud and rust?
What triumph in the blinding dust?
When intellect is bought and sold,
To buy a lie ten centuries old.

Awake, O mind, and break the spell!
Refuse the rhetoric of hell.
Shatter the glass of tribal pride,
Where reason goes to bleed and hide.
Unmask the idols made of brass
That mow down men like summer grass.

The highest peak the soul can scale
Is not where iron storm prevails,
But where the light of thought takes hold
To melt the cages, dark and cold.
Cast off the blindfold; claim the night—
And step into the human light.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
